Genomic DNA from each sample was isolated using the CTAB 
extraction protocol. Subsequently, 1 μg of genomic DNA was randomly 
sheared into approximately 350 bp fragments using a Covaris ultra­
sonicator. Library construction included end repair, A-tailing, adaptor 
ligation, purification, and PCR amplification. Initial library quantifica­
tion was performed using a Qubit 2.0 fluorometer, after which the li­
brary was diluted to 2 ng/μL. Insert size was evaluated using an Agilent 
2100 Bioanalyzer. After confirming the expected insert size, the effec­
tive library concentration was quantified by qPCR, with a threshold of 
>3 nM used to validate library quality. Qualified libraries were pooled 
according to effective concentration and the intended sequencing data 
volume, followed by paired-end sequencing using the Illumina platform 
with a PE150 strategy.

potential of microorganisms during AD, metagenomic sequencing of 
sludge samples was conducted at different stages (Days 0, 4, 17, and 38)

subjected to CDS prediction, and short segment contig sequences were 
filtered out. Non-redundant Unigene sets were generated via sequence

excerpt: Metagenomic sequencing was conducted to compare ARG profiles and methanogenesis-related metabolic potential in samples collected on days 21 and 49 of AD. Metagenomic DNA was paired-end sequenced on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform. After quality control, clean reads were assembled with MEGAHIT (v1.2.9), and contigs >500 bp were retained. ORFs were predicted using MetaGeneMark (v3.2.6), and coding sequences <100 nt were discarded. A non-redundant gene catalog was generated with CD-HIT (v4.6.1) (95% identity, 90% coverage), and clean reads were mapped back using Bowtie2 (v2.2.0) to estimate gene abundance. Predicted proteins were annotated against the NR_meta and KEGG (v87.1) databases using DIAMOND (v0.9.14), with emphasis on methanogenesis-related genes. ARGs were identified using ARG-OAP 3.0 with the SARG database (E-value < 1e-10, identity ≥ 80%, query coverage ≥ 80%) and normalized to 16S rRNA gene copy numbers. MGEs were quantified using the same criteria.
interpretation: DNA PE、组装/ORF和ARG流程支持实际宏基因组，无群落RNA建库。

Illumina-compatible sequencing li-
brary preparation for DNA samples was performed using NEXTFlex
DNA Sequencing Kit (Bioo Scientiﬁc) according to manufacturer
instructions. In brief, DNA shearing was performed to generate
fragments of approximately 200bp - 400bp size using CovarisS220
system (Life Technologies, USA). The fragment size distribution was
conﬁrmed on Agilent TapeStation with D1000 DNA Kit (Agilent,
Germany). Further, the sheared DNA was puriﬁed using HighPrep
beads (Magbio Genomics, USA) followed by end repair, A-tailing,
and ligation with the Illumina multiplexing adapters (Bioo Scien-
tiﬁc, Austin) according to the protocol outlined in NEXTFlex DNA
Sequencing kit. The ligated DNA was puriﬁed using HighPrep beads
and further subjected to 10 rounds of PCR (denaturation at 98 C for
2 min, cycling at 98 C for 30 sec, 65 C for 30 sec and 72 C for 60
sec, and ﬁnal extension at 72 C for 4 min) with Illumina compatible
primers provided within the kit. The resultant PCR product (Illu-
mina-compatible sequencing library) was puriﬁed using HighPrep
beads, quantiﬁed using Qubit ﬂuorometer and fragment size dis-
tribution analysis was performed on AgilentD1000 TapeStation.
KAPAqPCR quantiﬁcation kit (KAPA Biosystems; Massachusetts)
was used to quantify the Illumina-compatible sequencing library
prior to loading on Illumina Sequencer ﬂowcell.

section: Metagenomic sequencing of solid residues after anaerobic fermentation
excerpt:
Metagenomic sequencing was performed on solid resi­
dues obtained after anaerobic fermentation from different 
treatment groups. Total DNA was extracted using a fecal 
DNA extraction kit (D3141, Guangzhou Meiji Biotechnol­
ogy Co., China), and Illumina sequencing libraries were 
constructed and sequenced on the Novaseq 6000 platform 
with PE150 strategy [46]. After quality control of the raw 
data, Clean reads were obtained and assembled into contigs 
using MEGAHIT [17]. Protein-coding genes were predicted 
by MetaGeneMark, and a non-redundant gene catalog was 
constructed with CD-HIT [22]. Gene abundance was quan­
tified using Bowtie and PathoScope [9]. Functional anno­
tation was performed by aligning gene sequences against 
the KEGG, CAZy, and CARD databases with DIAMOND 
[32] to identify metabolic pathways, carbohydrate-active 
enzymes, and antibiotic resistance genes, respectively.
interpretation: 厌氧发酵后固体残渣总DNA/NovaSeq PE150、MEGAHIT/MetaGeneMark/非冗余基因及KEGG/CAZy/CARD确认MG；预处理阶段16S PE250单独区分。

excerpt:
The total genomic DNA of the samples was extracted by FastDNA 
SPIN kit for Soil (MP Biomedicals, USA), and the operation was strictly 
followed the instructions of the kit. The concentration and purity of the 
DNA were detected by NanoDrop spectrophotometer (NanoDrop ND- 
1000, Thermo Scientific, USA), and the integrity of the DNA was veri­
fied by 1% agarose gel electrophoresis. Metagenomic sequencing was 
performed by Majorbio, and the sequencing platform was Illumina 
HiSeq 2000. In order to construct the paired-end library construction, 
the genomic DNA was firstly broken to the average fragment length of 
about 400 bp by Covaris ultrasonicator (M220, Covaris Inc., USA). Then, 
the library was constructed by using NEXTFLEX™ Rapid DNA-Seq kit 
(Bioo Scientific, USA), and then amplified by bridge PCR, and then 
sequenced by using NovaSeq or HiSeq X reagent kits (Illumina, USA). 
The raw sequence data reported in this paper have been deposited in the 
NCBI database (PRJNA1438379).
